findings.claim: The --out containment check false-positives on legitimate in-root filenames beginning with '..' (e.g. --out ..foo.txt resolves inside root, but relative() returns '..foo.txt' which startsWith('..') matches, so a valid path is rejected). Conversely --out . yields relative '' which passes the check and only fails later at writeFile with EISDIR instead of a clean validation error.
findings.evidence: scripts/opencode-review.mjs:105-106 (outputRelative.startsWith('..') without a path-separator suffix check; no handling of outputRelative === '')

findings.claim: Containment is purely lexical; writeFile follows symlinks, so a symlink planted at <root>/out.json pointing outside --root defeats the '--out must stay inside --root' guarantee. No realpath resolution or O_NOFOLLOW is used.
findings.evidence: scripts/opencode-review.mjs:104,106 (resolve/relative check only) and scripts/opencode-review.mjs:147 (writeFile to the unresolved, symlink-following path)

findings.claim: diff_sha256 is a caller-asserted claim that is never verified against anything: the script never receives the diff, and context_sha256 hashes the claimed string itself rather than diff content. A prompt reviewing diff A invoked with diff B's hash produces a seat record attesting a review of diff B, indistinguishable from a genuine one. What component guarantees the prompt/diff-hash binding?
findings.evidence: scripts/opencode-review.mjs:53 (diff-sha256 validated as hex only), scripts/opencode-review.mjs:140 (diff_sha256 copied verbatim), scripts/opencode-review.mjs:141 (context_sha256 incorporates the claim, not the diff)

findings.claim: The response integrity check requires body.model to exactly equal the requested --model string. Many OpenAI-compatible gateways echo a provider-prefixed or version-suffixed model id; if opencode.ai does, every seat invocation fails with 'model does not match'. Confirm the endpoint echoes the exact requested id.
findings.evidence: scripts/opencode-review.mjs:132 (body?.model !== args.model strict inequality)

findings.claim: validateFinding accepts status 'accepted' for non-blocker findings, but the seat-record schema documents status as open|resolved only. The seat will emit records containing a status value outside the documented enum, which schema-validating downstream consumers will reject.
findings.evidence: scripts/opencode-review.mjs:70 (['open', 'resolved', 'accepted'].includes(finding.status)) vs. seat schema status: open|resolved

findings.claim: No consistency check between verdict and findings: a model response of verdict 'ready' carrying open blocker findings is emitted verbatim into the seat record. Either enforce the invariant here or document that consumers must re-derive the verdict.
findings.evidence: scripts/opencode-review.mjs:92 (verdict and findings returned independently, no cross-check), scripts/opencode-review.mjs:144-145 (both written to seat as-is)

findings.claim: The 2 MiB response cap is enforced only after response.text() has already buffered the entire body into memory, so the limit bounds processing, not memory consumption; a hostile or compromised endpoint can exhaust memory before the check runs.
findings.evidence: scripts/opencode-review.mjs:124 (await response.text() buffers fully) precedes scripts/opencode-review.mjs:125 (byte-length check)

findings.claim: The script requires Node >= 18 (global fetch) and >= 17.3 (AbortSignal.timeout) but declares no engines constraint and performs no feature guard; on older Node it fails at runtime with a bare 'fetch is not defined' message from the catch handler.
findings.evidence: scripts/opencode-review.mjs:110 (global fetch), scripts/opencode-review.mjs:121 (AbortSignal.timeout), scripts/opencode-review.mjs:151-154 (generic catch)

findings.claim: The seat record is written non-atomically; an interruption mid-writeFile leaves a truncated seat.json in the artifact directory that downstream aggregation could attempt to parse. Write to a temp file and rename for atomicity.
findings.evidence: scripts/opencode-review.mjs:147 (single writeFile directly to the final --out path)
